objective: Test whether the already frozen causal residual overlays improve raw trajectories from the object-disjoint MatPhys spring-proposal family.
claim_boundary: This is a matched post-open audit of already frozen PhysTwin-22 artifacts. It is not a fresh confirmation, an independent reproduction of published MatPhys, a calibration result, or a state-of-the-art claim.
matphys_interface: MatPhys proposes an object-disjoint spring field; the official PhysTwin/Warp backend produces the physical trajectory.

comparison.primary_subset: The eight cases whose frozen object-disjoint family selector chose a nonzero MatPhys spring proposal.
comparison.secondary_subset: All 22 cases, including 14 exact PhysTwin alpha-zero fallbacks.
comparison.online_supervision: The frozen overlay selector uses permitted prefix manual 3D tracks.

decision.reason: The Bayesian anchor improves the nonzero MatPhys subset on both point metrics, but the last-residual control has slightly lower aggregate point error.
decision.recommended_next_test: Freeze a genuinely fresh accepted-MatPhys cohort and compare raw MatPhys, last residual, Bayesian anchor, and calibrated predictive distributions without revisiting this opened cohort.
